Receivables advance (antecipação de vendas) lets you receive the value of credit-card sales, either lump-sum or installment, before the normal settlement date, so you don't have to wait for the usual clearing period to get the money in your account [8].

- **Timing:** A sales schedule becomes available for advance from D+1 (one business day after the sale). It stays available until D-3 (three business days before the schedule settles into your account) [6].
- **Cards:** Some card brands can't be advanced through Getnet. For those you have to go through the brand's own operator [6].
- **Normal receiving options:** Debit sales are available the next day. For credit, you can choose to receive everything in 2 days, in 30 days, or month by month following the card installments [7].
- **Automatic Advance:** This is a condition for the exemption on the "Receba Conforme suas Vendas" plan. It goes through credit approval, and Getnet assesses each contract individually [3].
- **Gravame:** If you use your receivables as collateral for a loan, the receivables schedule is directed to the lender to guarantee the operation [2]. Sales then go to your Get Conta, up to the outstanding loan balance [1].

The passages I found don't give a fee or rate for a standard advance, and they don't say how to request one.

Up to 48 installments, according to the Crediário page [1][5]. The installment limit is set by each card issuer under its own credit policies [3]. Interest rates can also vary by issuer [1].

At the card machine, you can simulate the installments and interest by going to credit > crediário. You can also print the simulation receipt if the machine has paper [3]. The simulation is for reference only and depends on credit analysis, and the issuer decides whether to approve the transaction [3].

Receivables advance (antecipação de vendas) lets you receive credit-card sales early instead of waiting for the normal settlement date. It covers single-payment and installment credit sales [sup-duvidas-12].

- **Timing:** You can advance a sales schedule from D+1, which is one business day after the sale. It stays available until D-3, which is three business days before the money would reach your account [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10].
- **Card brands:** For some brands, you can't advance through Getnet. You can only do it with that brand's own operator [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10].
- **Automatic advance:** It is a condition for the fee exemption on the "Receba Conforme suas Vendas" plan. It goes through credit approval, and Getnet assesses each contract individually [sup-duvidas-100].
- **Liens and loans:** A lien (gravame) on your receivables sends your receivables schedule to the bank that holds the loan [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-02]. For a Getnet loan, your sales are received in your Get Conta, up to the outstanding loan balance [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-05].
- **E-commerce:** Advancing e-commerce sales stays blocked for 6 months. Physical-store sales can still be advanced normally [sup-link-de-pagamento-12].
